thread.title: Analog Devices, Another Mini Texas Instruments - Analog Devices (NASDAQ:ADI)

author: Shareholders Unite
title: Analog Devices, Another Mini Texas Instruments - Analog Devices (NASDAQ:ADI)
text:
We argued recently that Skyworks ( SWKS ) is a sort of mini (and much cheaper) Texas Instruments ( TXN ), in the sense of having a few similar characteristics like:
Secular growth. Deep and wide capabilities. Producing for niche markets with little competition. Enjoying substantial margins and cash flows, much of which is returned to shareholders. The comparison wasn't perfect, we admitted (Skyworks is cheaper for a reason, like its dependence on Apple ( AAPL )) but a helpful commenter suggested Analog Devices ( ADI ) was a better fit. Indeed, in quite a number of ways it is, but it's also substantially more expensive than Skyworks.
You might want to ask what our obsession with Texas Instruments is, well, we have argued that it's an almost ideal company for investors, so it serves as a sort of benchmark. So we were looking whether we could find similar companies and we ended up with Skyworks and now Analog Devices.
Growth ADI Revenue (TTM) data by YCharts
The company has experienced a tremendous increase in growth and operational performance the last two years, also on the back of acquisitions.
Growth is helped by favorable technology trends, especially in communications with much of the innovation in 5G in the radio subsystems which plays right in the capabilities of the company ( Q4CC ):
given the increasing demands for spectral space thermal and cost efficiency, our comprehensive portfolio of software-defined, mixed signal, RF, microwave and power management technologies will enable ADI to create even more compelling solutions for our customers in the years ahead.
The B2B market consists of Industrial (the largest segment responsible for 49% of revenues with sectors like healthcare, aerospace and defense), Automotive and Communications. B2B revenue grew 13% y/y in Q4.
While healthcare (X-Ray imaging) grew double-digits, there was a slowdown in factory automation, surprisingly from China.
The biggest driver of growth here is the communications sector (22% of revenue), which increased almost 30% in Q4 (up from mid-20s in Q3). It is mainly driven by enhanced build-out of 4G and the early stages of 5G.
The company is increasing content at customers and this will likely increase further with 5G with massive MIMO and millimeter wave. Massive MIMO will increase the potential for its content four-fold and when millimeter wave hits, content will potentially increase more than 10-fold over 4G. From the Q4CC :
Much of the innovation of 5G’s systems is taking place in the radio subsystem, given the increasing demands for spectral space thermal and cost efficiency, our comprehensive portfolio of software defined, mixed signal, RF, microwave and power management technologies will enable ADI to create even more compelling solutions for our customers in the years ahead... And indeed massive MIMO is just a stepping stone to millimeter wave based future generations. Here carriers will look to increase the radio channel count up to 512 channels per radio and we are very well positioned to once again solve these immense radio challenges with our comprehensive cutting edge portfolio. So I believe we are really in the early stages of a multiyear growth cycle in this particular space.
Automotive is 15% of revenues and grew in the low single business. The company produces solutions for BMS, radar, lidar, IMU, essential for ADAS. The company has been doing well in cabin electronics but experienced problems in its battery management solution.
But management argues that these latter problems are now behind it and it expects growth in this sector to return to at least the high single-digits.
Healthcare (X-Ray imaging) and audio processing are also growing double-digits.
While its consumer market is just 13% of sales (mostly sockets in mobile phones), it is one sector that has been declining (10-20% in 2018).
Acquisitions The massive $14.8B acquisition of LTC in the summer of 2016 is bearing fruit. The company has made much progress with the integration of LTC with $150M in synergies already achieved and another $100M still reachable.
Management argues that the cross-selling opportunity has doubled in value since the Analyst Day. Management is confident it is able to double LTC's revenue growth over the next few years.
The company bought German radar technology solutions provider Symeo this year to boost its position in automotive markets. It also bought OtoSense , a specialist in sound recognition this year.
Guidance Q1 guidance is a little complicated by the fact that the previous Q1 quarter was a 14-week quarter (rather than the usual 13) and the company is adopting the new ASC 606 accounting standard. So Q1 guidance is normalized to take account of the 14 weeks:
Revenue will be $1.51B midpoint (both in ASC 605 as 606), 7% above Q1 2018. Gross margins decline sequentially to 70.8% due to normal shutdowns (holidays) and business mix. Operating expenses will be $450M (midpoint) with operating margins at 41%. Diluted earnings per share will be $1.28 +/- 7 cents. The company's B2B book-to-bill ratio is actually below 1, driven largely by the industrial sector. The company hasn't experienced this for some time, but management argues that it is concentrated in two segments, factory automation (Chinese demand) and automated test equipment.
Management doesn't yet call the bottom in both, even if it saw some sequential improvements in October. It argues it's more of a pause than something more fundamental, caused by some macro uncertainty.
On the other hand, the guidance still implies the eight consecutive quarter of double-digit B2B growth, so it doesn't look to be that serious.
Management also argues that it hasn't seen much impact of tariffs, nor much (if any) pull-in from Chinese buyers to beat the implementation of additional tariffs. It does see caution in long-term plans though.
Margins The company enjoys some terrific margins:
ADI Gross Profit Margin (Quarterly) data by YCharts
These are GAAP margins, the non-GAAP operating margin is substantially better at a record 43%.
The company has a long-run model in with gross margin at 70%+ and operating margin at 39-45%.
What enables the company to enjoy such tremendous margins (and the associated cash flow, see below)?
The nature of the products which are, on the whole, very specialist (at the other end of commodity products) with little competition. The nature of the end markets, which are mostly industrial customers where competition is less cut-throat. The company refocused strategy on the B2B sector a decade ago and this has clearly paid off. A decade of investing heavily in R&D and capabilities, just under 20% of revenue (see below). 95% of the R&D efforts are directed at the B2B sector. Adding capabilities and synergies through acquisitions (like that of LTC, Linear and Hittite). ADI R&D to Revenue (TTM) data by YCharts
Cash ADI Cash from Operations (TTM) data by YCharts
What happened in 2018 is that cash flow basically doubled from previous years and we are surprised not more of this has been seeping through into the stock price.
It's of course quite something for a company operating on $6B of revenue to produce over $2B in free cash flow (35% of revenues). Even a 4% rise in inventories in Q4 didn't mar this picture.
The cash flow has enabled the company to rapidly deleverage, reducing its debt by $1.5B in 2018:
ADI Net Debt Issuance (TTM) data by YCharts
And even before this bumper cash year the company wasn't exactly a slouch, having returned $10B to shareholders since 2005. Now that leverage has been cut to much more modest levels, management is promising to return all free cash flow to shareholders.
We don't think that is incorporated in the share price either, curious. The company even pays a dividend with the shares yielding 1.92%.
The company does still have a substantial long-term debt though ($6.26B) and $816M of cash.
Tax issue Ireland argues that the company must pay $49M in taxes from transfer payments going back to 2013, and this excludes fines and interest so the figure could be substantially higher.
The company is going to fight this, but the outcome is anything but guaranteed and management argued that if it loses the case it will have a "material impact."
Valuation ADI P/E Ratio (TTM) data by YCharts
Compare this with Skyworks and Texas Instruments (for the sake of reducing clutter, in a separate graph):
TXN P/E Ratio (TTM) data by YCharts
Basically, Analog Devices is the most expensive stock on all metrics, which at first sight is a little surprising to us. One could say it's a sort of super Texas Instruments.
We think the main reason for the valuation difference is the better growth prospects that Analog Devices has at the moment.
Analysts expect revenues to grow from $6.51B this year to $6.98B in 2019 and EPS to rise from $0.46 to $0.63 in the same time. For Texas Instruments these expectations are revenues declining from $15.81B in 2018 to $15.53B in 2019 and EPS from $5.57 to $5.54 in the same period.
Skyworks is expected to raise revenues from $3.91B in fiscal 2019 (starting next February) to $4.21B in fiscal 2020 and EPS from $7.34 to $8.16 over the same period.
Conclusion We think that Analog Devices is a terrific company, producing terrific margins and cash flow. After having substantially deleveraged, that cash flow is now set to benefit shareholders even more, as management will return 100% of free cash flow to them, which is 6.6% of the market cap at present, or a staggering 35% of revenues.
The company looks also set to grow substantially from the introduction of 5G; even if its communications sector is just over a fifth of revenues, this is likely to increase substantially.
While Analog Devices is indeed more like Texas Instruments than Skyworks, the shares are also substantially more expensive, we therefore still have a slight preference for the latter.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
